standard_prerequisites.name: Invariant elements b of (R/JR)^G lift to elements of R^G modulo the ideal generated by J, with a monic polynomial relation
For x in R^G the polynomial prod (T - sigma(x)) lies in the ideal generated by T - x and hence its reduction modulo J is determined by x mod J
An integral ring map inducing purely inseparable residue field extensions induces homeomorphisms on spectra

core_obligations: Part (1) follows from the polynomial lifting lemma applied to the ideal JR: every invariant b in (R/JR)^G is the image of an element of R^G modulo JR, so a monic polynomial P over R^G/J with image (T - b)^n exists (proof lines 32619-32619). For part (2), an element a in the kernel is the image of x in R^G intersect JR; the norm factorization (T - x)^n = prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(x)) is congruent to T^n modulo J because each sigma(x) - x lies in JR, by the polynomial-in-ideal lemma (proof lines 32620-32623). The ring map R^G/J -> (R/JR)^G is therefore integral with purely inseparable residue field extensions, and the universally-bijective lemma of the algebra chapter gives the homeomorphisms on spectra (proof lines 32624-32625).
proof_roadmap: Derive part (1) from the polynomial lifting lemma with I = JR (proof lines 32619-32619).
Derive part (2) from the norm factorization and the polynomial-in-ideal lemma, then the spectral statement from universal bijectivity (proof lines 32620-32625).
